findings.problem: This story card is not the opening card but has 3 sentences: the quote from Luke 16:3, "Friend, I KNOW that feeling." and "One day you're in the drawer, the next you're shoved behind the takeout menus."

rule.text: Every other story card is 1 to 2 sentences.

findings.problem: The quote "I know what I will do," adds a comma that is not in the BSB. Luke 16:4 reads 'I know what I will do so that after my removal...' with no comma after "do".

rule.text: Quotation marks around Bible words mean the exact BSB wording, punctuation included. A paraphrase uses no quotation marks.

findings.problem: This story card has 3 sentences: "So he calls in each one of his master's debtors." "Everybody who owes the boss." "He starts with the first one: ..."

rule.text: Every other story card is 1 to 2 sentences.

findings.problem: This choice card follows a choice card (card 8). Its setup (the manager tells the debtor to take his bill, sit down quickly and write) is only in the question. No story card tells it.

rule.text: The setup for a choice is always on a story card.

findings.problem: This story card has 4 sentences and two separate moments: a reaction to Luke 16:6, then the second debtor in Luke 16:7. It also switches tense ("asks" then "he replied"), and the second "he" could mean either the manager or the debtor.

rule.text: Every other story card is 1 to 2 sentences.

findings.problem: Story card 12 gives no context that points to the right answer (the master commends the manager). Its joke leans the other way ("this mustache would be standing straight up"), so a thoughtful baker would reason toward the wrong answers.

rule.text: Before each choice card, Papa Dorin's story card gives enough context that the baker can reason their way to the answer.

findings.problem: Most choice cards in stop 1 are discovery questions the baker can't reason out: card 4 (digging or begging), card 8 (olive oil), card 9 (fifty), card 11 (eighty, not fifty), card 13 (commends) and card 15 (which group is more shrewd). Only cards 2 and 6 are clearly informed guesses.

rule.text: A few of those are okay, as long as most choice cards are informed guesses.

findings.problem: This story card has 4 sentences (the quote, "And He doesn't pretend...", "Money's like a fresh cookie...", "It does NOT last.").

rule.text: Every other story card is 1 to 2 sentences.

findings.problem: The quote "I tell you, use worldly wealth to make friends for yourselves." ends with a period that is not in the BSB at that point (Luke 16:9 goes on with "so that when it is gone").

rule.text: Quotation marks around Bible words mean the exact BSB wording, punctuation included. A paraphrase uses no quotation marks.

findings.problem: This is a which-thing/where question, but the wrong answer "Houses of gold" is not a real detail from the Bible. It is made up.

rule.text: For who, which thing and where questions, wrong answers are real details from somewhere in the Bible, like Joppa when the right answer is Tarshish.

findings.problem: This story card has 3 sentences: the quote with "and then He flips it around", "Little things count, friend." and "I got my stamp right one crooked cookie at a time."

rule.text: Every other story card is 1 to 2 sentences.

findings.problem: This story card has 3 sentences. It also says "This time it isn't about money," which decides how Luke 16:11 (worldly wealth) and 16:12 (belongings of another) connect. The text doesn't say that.

rule.text: Leave open what the text leaves open: who is being spoken to, why, or how two things connect.

findings.problem: Stop 2 (Luke 16:9-13) is direct teaching, not story. Card 8 blanks the exact wording of Luke 16:12 ("another", "own"). The docs apply the no-guessing-wording and fewer-choice-cards rules only to poetry, letters and prophecy. They say nothing about teaching sections inside a parable passage.
findings.question: Should teaching sections in Parables passages (like Jesus' sayings in Luke 16:9-13) follow the poetry/letters/prophecy rules (no guessing the wording, fewer choice cards, up to 4 story cards in a row)?
